title: Light Herbal Snappy Canadian Duck Legs Confit
description: A diabetic-friendly, herb-infused dish featuring succulent duck legs, perfect for a weeknight dinner. Inspired by Canadian cuisine, this recipe balances flavors and textures for a delightful meal.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 2755 F (1355 C).
Season the duck legs with salt and black pepper.
In a small saucepan, combine olive oil, garlic, thyme, and rosemary. Heat over low heat for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Place the duck legs in a large Dutch oven or oven-safe pot, skin side up. Brush the herb-infused oil over the duck legs, making sure they are fully coated.
Cover the pot with a lid and transfer to the preheated oven. Braise the duck legs for 2 hours, or until tender and easily shredded with a fork.
Remove the pot from the oven and let it cool slightly. Strain the juices and discard the solids.
Shred the duck legs with two forks and serve warm, garnished with chopped parsley and a squeeze of lemon juice.
Refrigerate the confit for at least 2 hours or overnight to allow the flavors to meld and the meat to set.
